searchText: I think algo type should be a distinct field rather than a byte in a blob. What if we have more than 55 types? (maybe not in 10 years, but plausable in 100 years) going to 56 locks us into a 256 cap, and allowing a free int allows for smantic meanings in the nubmers, such as using FIPS numbers like 204 (0xcc) for MLDSA and doing <algo><security category> would make useful things like 2042, 2043, and 2045 for the three key strengths of MLDSA. (And key strengths will easily chew up algos, apart from curves and whatever happens with zk standards) Also a nit, primary signature sould be last. when processing bytes linearly you calc the hash then have the hash ready for the signature. That's why some FIPs formats have salt before the signature fields in signatures like Falcon. If we’d have algorithm sub-types, we could have each algorithm handle those subtypes, this’ll leave it up to the algorithm to decide how to encode subtypes. Also, once we do get to the 256 cap, it wouldn’t be all that hard to implement something along the lines of a pseudo-algorithm for extending the algorithm space to a uint16 or greater. yeah, the point being, that _changing_ a field to suddenly mean something else is breaking. so, just packing it into the ProgressiveByteList leaves open this design space. like, if we define it as a uint8, the reality will be that this will eventually become some magic, that then indicates that another location should be examined for more distinguishing factors xD but yeah, numbering scheme is obviously open. could also do a 3 byte fips/secp/256k1 prefix, many options https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10720 have moved the signature _outside_ the union as well. This should make live easier for 7932, I guess? also means, signature now covers the union selector makes more sense, overall, as this cleanly separates the tx data from the signature It would make life significantly easier for SSZ <-> 7932 interaction and is a lot cleaner. I have a draft PR for some of the 7932 tweaks readyish https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10721#issuecomment-3491103680 OK, taking this one in. and then also doing 6493 as followup https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/10722 this one is the bump for 6493 to support the progressivecontainer and setcode transaction Do you think a formal registry definition would be a good idea? I.e. ‘dict[uint8,…..]’ like in 6404. if it's concise. executable code is good for testing, and avoids ambiguity. but it shouldn't be an elaborate framework that distracts from the relevant parts of the EIP tricky thing of setcode is that authorizations are a bit like.. nested transactions, so the combo of an SSZ transaction that contains a converted RLP authorization also exists xD but it's kinda straight-forward have looked at it / commented structure-wise, maybe the registry first, and the RLP wrapper below (as an option, if 6404 doesn't make the race) Thanks for the comments, I am sort of stumped with EIP-155 as drafting an exception specifically for it seems wrong and it is somewhat useless when wrapped because of the chain id in the wrapper. if this is only relevant in the RLP case but not SSZ, maybe fine to just sketch it out and leave it as an open question I’ll leave it as an open question as the v override only affects the RLP wrapper. The SSZ world is so much simpler. anyway, feel free to make a PR that bumps 6404 to link to the registry, when it's ready. the entire secp256 section can probably be moved over, cleaning up 6404 to be focused on just the transactions and nothing else I'll make a PR when it is done this seems to be better but like the origin form where we had 2 unions with one outer union holding the rlp signature stuff one for ssz seems best and that was also compatible with the new ones with ProgressiveList[byte] no need for a union on signatures, it's semantically the same but uses fewer hashes it's secp256k1 sig btw, the native SSZ sig in 6493 uses the same. only compute_sig_hash differs ah yes progressivelist[byte] would solve the signature ambiguity ill try to get my fork bumped to latest 6404 and 6466 version b4 devconnect for the demo test vectors https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/blob/master/assets/eip-6404/convert_tests.py Thnx ! I had a look into these and have been working on a branch different than the one I have a pr at Nim-eth for https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/1781#issuecomment-3493852905
